source_text: Manifestum erat non generationis, sed alterius cuiuscumque fuisse causae, quod unius generantis peccato apud iniquum tamen iudicem filii videbantur obnoxii.
pass_a_gloss: It was manifest that it was not of generation, but of some other cause, that by the sin of one generating the sons seemed liable—yet before an unjust judge.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: It would therefore be clear that it was not generation but some other cause that made children appear liable for the sin of this one parent—before an unjust judge, however.

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
